title: Nasal polyp removal
what: Working through the nose, the surgeon removes the polyps with a thin camera and instruments. Usually there are no cuts on the face.
why: When polyps block breathing through the nose, reduce your sense of smell, or cause frequent sinus infections, and medicines do not help.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 minutes to 2 hours; usually 1 to 3 days in hospital, or home the same day
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to do
Any problems with anesthesia in you or relatives

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need a CT scan of the sinuses, blood tests, and an ECG. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you.

prepare.title: Food and drink
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, tissues, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: Your referral, scans, and test results
Things for a 1 to 3 day hospital stay
steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
Anesthesia is given, and you fall asleep
The surgeon puts a thin camera into your nose
The polyps are removed with special instruments
Sometimes packing is placed in the nose
You wake up in the recovery room
feel: Your nose is blocked, so you breathe through your mouth
A dull ache and heavy head, and bloody fluid from the nose in the first days
after: Packing usually comes out after 1 to 2 days
Do not blow your nose hard until your doctor says it is OK
Use rinses and sprays as prescribed
No heavy lifting, saunas, or hot baths for a couple of weeks
Polyps can come back. The treatment your doctor prescribes matters
red_flags: Heavy bleeding from the nose or into the throat: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or a severe headache
Swelling around the eye, or worse vision: see a doctor urgently
Clear, watery fluid from the nose after surgery: tell your doctor

faq.a: Sometimes. To make it less likely, your doctor will prescribe treatment after surgery.

faq.q: Will my sense of smell come back?
faq.a: It often gets better, but not always right away.

reminders.text: Nose surgery tomorrow. Pack your things and documents. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
